claims.statement: AA Coding Agents Index (equal-weight mean of DeepSWE v1.1, SWE-Atlas-QnA and Terminal-Bench v4, each agent in its own harness), same page snapshot as artificial-analysis-coding-agents-muse-wonder-2026-10-13.json (all 88 stored peer values re-checked equal): Antigravity CLI with Gemini 4 Argon (high) 63.76 at $5.84 per task (AA default configuration), against Claude Code Sonnet 5.5 (max) 68.36 ($14.19), Muse Code Muse Wonder Full 68.03, Claude Code Opus 5.5 (max) 65.99 ($13.04), Muse Code Muse Wonder 63.50 ($8.05), Codex GPT-6.1 Sol (xhigh) 62.91 ($1.04), Claude Code Fable 5.1 (max) 62.22 ($12.39), Codex GPT-6 Astra (max) 61.65 ($7.47). Argon is 4th of the stored roster on the Index and the cheapest per task among the five rows above 63 (Muse Wonder Full has no cost). DeepSWE v1.1 on this run: Argon 78.76%, Muse Wonder Full 77.0%, Sol xhigh 73.2%, Sonnet 5.5 72.0%, Opus 5.5 68.4%. SWE-Atlas-QnA Argon 56.45%; Terminal-Bench v4 (this run) Argon 56.06%.

CONFLICT, not reconciled: Google's blog says Argon 'sets a new state of the art on DeepSWE v1.1 (77.9%)'. AA's own DeepSWE v1.1 run through the Antigravity CLI gives Argon 78.76%, i.e. 0.9 points above Google's figure, and Muse Wonder Full 77.0% (Meta's launch table: 79.0 for Muse Wonder Full, 78.8 for Muse Wonder; see the Meta files). The Datacurve DeepSWE board has no Argon row and was last updated 2026-09-22 (see the coverage file). The three sources use different harnesses and dates.
